## My Thinking

My family has worked this land in Quzhou for as long as I can remember. I have about 8 mu of flat field, same as most people in the village. I never went to school, but I know the land. I watch what my neighbors do, I listen to my husband, and I go by what has worked before.

Here in Quzhou there are two crops every year — winter wheat, then summer corn. That is just how it is. The soil is flat and good for it, the irrigation wells are there, and the grain buyers in town expect it. I would not change this. My mother grew wheat and corn, I grow wheat and corn.

**Wheat** goes in around Hanlu — early October. I will buy improved seed from the shop in town, the kind most people in the village are using this year. Before planting I will run the rotary tiller over the field. I put down phosphate-potassium compound fertilizer and some urea as base fertilizer, then top-dress again with urea at jointing when the stalks start reaching up. I water before winter freezes the ground, again at jointing, and again at heading. That is three times. In spring I spray once for aphids and powdery mildew, and I spray herbicide earlier when the weeds are small. One more spray later if I need it.

**Corn** goes in right after wheat harvest in June — no time to waste. I use hybrid seed, the kind the dealer pushes. I do not plow again because the wheat stubble is still on the ground and there is no time — I run the rotary over it quickly and plant. I put in compound fertilizer at planting and top-dress with urea at big bell stage when the plant is knee-high. If it rains enough I only water once or twice. I spray once for corn borer and once for weeds if they get bad.

I do not expect to try anything new this year. New things cost money and if they fail I cannot recover. I will do what I know.
